The motors remained enabled at the end; closing the episode is not the same as a physical stop.

manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.

Task description: Hang the white handled cup on the left side of the wooden cup rack so the rack bar passes through the cup handle opening and supports the cup.

Success criteria: The cup has been picked up, its handle is looped over one of the rack’s bars and supported by it, leaving the cup suspended above the table without relying on the gripper for support.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping a mug-wall section away from the handle with ample outer clearance, one finger inside and one outside and pads below the rim, leaving room to thread the handle onto the rod. Limit the opening to the wall and necessary entry clearance.
- Before closing, confirm that the fingers are actually on the inside and outside of the cup wall rather than resting only against the rim. If it needs another grasp, first set the cup base back on the table for support.
- Adjust the cup in an open area away from the rack so the handle hole faces the tip of the chosen hanging bar. This reduces the risk of the cup body brushing the post or neighboring bar when rotating the wrist near the rack.
- As the rod passes through the handle opening, make small adjustments along the rod direction and watch clearance between the cup and post to avoid the cup hitting the rack first and pushing the base.
- Confirm the handle has passed the rod tip and is supported by the rod body before gradually unloading the gripper. If handle and rod only overlap in the image, inspect from another angle to avoid a fall after release.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start this authorized real-robot episode with the specified parameters and follow the returned manual and live observations; when finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

I have read the manual and confirmed only the right arm is available. The cup is to the left of the rack. I am adjusting the approach pose to grip the cup's sidewall near its opening while leaving room for the handle to pass onto the rod.

The approach hit a wrist joint limit, reported as a recoverable rejection. I lowered the height using the new measured position and restored motion. Next I will narrow the opening and gradually align with the cup wall.

The gripper is near the cup opening, and the cup wall lies within the projected area between the fingers. I am lowering in increments of no more than 1 cm and checking finger placement with both cameras.

Both cameras show the outer finger outside the cup and the inner finger facing inside; the cup remains stable on the table. I will lower slightly so the pads pass the rim, close, and first check with a short lift.

After a short lift, the cup rose with the gripper, whose opening remains approximately 2.6 mm, with no further sliding observed yet. I will adjust the wrist pose, lift the cup higher, and approach the rod on the left of the rack.

The cup is clearly off the table and remains securely grasped. The wrist camera now shows the tip of the left rod. I will continue aligning with the handle opening through small lateral steps and confirm insertion before removing gripper support.

The cup handle and bar tip are at similar heights in the wrist view, and the rack base does not appear to have shifted. Front-back position still needs confirmation; image overlap alone is not enough to judge whether the cup is hooked on.

Near the outside of the handle, the cup turned slightly, and insertion through the hole is still unconfirmed. I backed away a little and will correct its front-back position and height before approaching again.

There is still some occlusion near the handle opening, so support of the cup by the rod has not been confirmed. I am making further millimeter-level height and lateral adjustments while keeping the gripper closed.

The wrist view now shows the rod tip beginning to enter the handle opening, but the insertion depth still needs confirmation. I will make a small adjustment along the rod and lower gradually to check support.

The rod is visible passing through the handle hole in the main view, and the rack has not moved. I am lowering slowly so the handle rests against the rod, then will gradually relax the gripper to see whether it hangs independently.
After release, the cup is hanging by its handle from the bar, clear of the gripper and suspended above the table. I will withdraw a little farther, check its stability, and end the episode.
